rules.title: San Francisco Just Cause Eviction Requirements
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant only for one of 17 enumerated just-cause reasons, which must be the dominant motive for eviction. Mere expiration of a rental agreement or change of ownership does not constitute just cause. The 17 reasons include: non-payment or habitual late payment of rent; failure to cure a substantial breach; nuisance or substantial interference with comfort, safety, or enjoyment (severe, continuing or recurring); illegal use of the unit (but not single cured violation of short-term rental law within 30 days); tenant's refusal to execute a written extension under materially same terms; tenant's refusal to allow landlord access as required by law; only tenant is unapproved subtenant; owner-occupancy or occupancy by immediate family member; good-faith sale following approved condo conversion; demolition or permanent removal from housing use; capital improvements making unit temporarily uninhabitable with reoccupancy after; substantial rehabilitation of building at least 50 years old and essentially uninhabitable (work cost at least 75% of new construction); withdrawal under Ellis Act; lead remediation required by Health Code; demolition under development agreement; expiration of Good Samaritan occupancy agreement with notice within 60 days; or completion of development project requiring demolition. Landlord also needs just cause to remove housing services (garage, parking, storage, laundry), though may temporarily remove parking and storage for mandatory soft-story seismic retrofit if requirements met.
rules.quotedSpan: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction. Note that the mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute "just cause" for eviction.
rules.coverageDescription: All rental units covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance, including some units exempt from rent increase limitations (newly constructed units with Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979; units eligible for rent increase under Costa-Hawkins Act; units where rent regulated by another government agency).
